evals.prompt: The team wants this line in CHANGELOG.md (v2.4 entry) rewritten before release: “This groundbreaking update leverages cutting-edge systems to provide a seamless experience, ensuring users can effortlessly enjoy robust performance.”
evals.expected_output: Produce shorter, specific prose without puffery or invented detail.
assertions: Removes the promotional phrases "groundbreaking", "cutting-edge", "seamless" and "effortlessly"
Removes unsupported promotional claims without adding unsupported specifics; if no concrete fact is supplied, uses accurate neutral wording or notes the limitation
The rewritten sentence itself is shorter than the supplied original; any explanation is brief and clearly separate

evals.prompt: Make clearer for technical docs: “The configuration is loaded by the service when it is started.”
evals.expected_output: Use active voice and retain meaning.
assertions: Service is grammatical subject
Uses active verb such as loads
Preserves startup timing and configuration

evals.prompt: Our data retention page (evals/files/retention-policy.md) is way too wordy for the internal wiki. Tighten it up.
evals.expected_output: A shorter policy that keeps: exports must be deleted within `RETENTION_DAYS`; unless under an active legal hold, which must not be deleted until legal releases it; teams should use the `export-purge` job wherever reasonably possible (manual deletions are not in the audit log); authorised staff may request a one-off extension of up to 30 days via the DATA queue; the portal message "Export blocked: legal hold active" quoted exactly, with the outcome that the download does not proceed. en-GB spellings kept. No change log or word counts appended.
assertions: The deletion rule is still a must-level requirement tied to `RETENTION_DAYS`, and the legal-hold exception is kept, including that held exports must not be deleted until the legal team releases the hold
The `export-purge` recommendation stays should-level: it is not dropped and not turned into a bare imperative or a must
Keeps the feasibility qualifier on the `export-purge` recommendation ("wherever reasonably possible" or an equivalent such as "where possible")
The extension stays a permission (may or equivalent) for authorised staff, with the 30-day limit and the DATA queue
`RETENTION_DAYS`, `export-purge` and the message "Export blocked: legal hold active" appear verbatim
Keeps the blocked-download outcome: when the message shows, the download does not proceed
Keeps the source's en-GB spellings (for example "authorised") rather than switching to en-US
The rewrite is shorter than the original and drops the throat-clearing such as "It is important to note that"
Returns the rewritten policy without an appended list of changes or word counts

evals.prompt: Put this in active voice for the postmortem: “The feature flag was disabled at 14:05 UTC, and the cache was flushed shortly after.”
evals.expected_output: Keeps the passive (or another actor-free wording) because the source names no actor, and says so in one short line; keeps both events and 14:05 UTC.
assertions: Does not name an actor (an engineer, the on-call, a team, a system) that the source does not name
Keeps both events, their order, and the time 14:05 UTC
Explains in one short line that the source names no actor, so active voice would invent one, or asks who performed the actions

evals.prompt: can you make this shorter? “Never force-push to `main`.”
evals.expected_output: Returns the sentence unchanged with a short note that it is already minimal.
assertions: Keeps the negation, the force-push action and `main` verbatim
Does not return a version that drops the negation, the action or the branch just to be shorter
Says briefly that the sentence is already minimal

evals.prompt: Here's our README (evals/files/brand-readme.md). Marketing wants to keep the playful brand voice, but can you point out where it's wordy?
evals.expected_output: Numbered suggestions only, each quoting an original fragment with a proposed replacement and a reason; no rewritten README or section; commands untouched.
assertions: Does not return a rewritten README or a rewritten section in place of the original
Gives numbered suggestions, each quoting a fragment of the original and proposing replacement text
No suggestion changes `brew install pocketbrew` or `pocketbrew sync --dry-run`
No suggestion adds a feature, metric or contact that the README does not state

evals.prompt: Write the error message our CLI prints when the user's API token has expired. They fix it by running `acme login`.
evals.expected_output: A one- or two-sentence message: the token expired, run `acme login` to sign in again. No invented lifetime, URL or contact.
assertions: States that the API token has expired
Tells the user to run `acme login`, verbatim
Does not invent a token lifetime, URL, support contact or error code
The message leads with what failed and what to do, with no apology, preamble or puffery

evals.prompt: can you tighten this up? it's going in the release notes
evals.expected_output: One short line asking for the text to tighten; no invented sample and no rewrite.
assertions: Asks the user to supply the text to tighten
Does not invent sample release-note text or present a rewrite of text that was not supplied

evals.prompt: Tighten this case study for the blog: evals/files/case-study.md
evals.expected_output: The surrounding prose is shorter (Fernwood Logistics, Leeds, Formline, start of the 2025 financial year, nine to three working days, rollout to warehouse staff kept); Priya Nair's quotation is reproduced word for word; any suggestion about the quotation comes after the rewrite as a numbered suggestion, not applied.
assertions: Priya Nair's quotation appears word for word as in the source, including "basically drowning in paper" and "really, really great"
The prose outside the quotation is shorter and drops filler such as "It is worth mentioning that" and "At the present time"
Keeps the facts: Leeds, Formline, the start of the 2025 financial year, nine to three working days, and the rollout to warehouse staff
Any suggestion to shorten the quotation is listed after the rewrite as a separate suggestion and is not applied to the quoted text

evals.prompt: write the empty-state copy for our Saved Searches page in our brand voice
evals.expected_output: Short plain copy for an empty Saved Searches page (no saved searches yet), with no invented tone and no invented button or menu names, ending with `Needs: a sample of the brand voice` (other Needs lines allowed for missing product details).
assertions: Gives short empty-state copy saying there are no saved searches yet
The copy is plain: it does not invent a tone such as jokes, slang, emoji or exclamation-heavy enthusiasm
Ends with a `Needs:` line asking for a sample of the brand voice
Does not name a button, menu path or feature the prompt does not give, unless it is marked with a `Needs:` line

evals.prompt: evals/files/setup-guide.md repeats itself. Clean it up and merge the duplicate install sections.
evals.expected_output: One install section that keeps `pip install ledgerline`, the Python 3.9 condition requiring `pip install "pip<24"` first, and the `ledgerline --version` check; the database section kept with its heading; a note naming the removed or renamed heading and its old anchor.
assertions: Produces a single install section instead of two
The merged section keeps the Python 3.9 condition and the exact command `pip install "pip<24"`, with must-level force
Keeps `pip install ledgerline`, `ledgerline --version` and `LEDGERLINE_DB_URL` verbatim
Keeps the "Configuring the database" heading and its facts
Adds a note naming the heading that was removed or renamed (and so its anchor)

evals.prompt: A database query takes 800 ms on 10,000 rows. Explain likely causes and how to profile it; do not copyedit my wording.
evals.expected_output: Provide technical diagnosis and concrete profiling evidence, not copyediting.
assertions: Discusses profiling or execution plan evidence
Does not merely rewrite prompt
Does not assert unverified cause as fact
